name: Arberth

attributes.attribute: a magical fairy mound where people see visions

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Arberth is a Welsh mythological site. The name belongs to a magical fairy mound in the kingdom of Pwyll. People went there to see visions. Some scholars associate the mound with the town of Narberth in Dyfed, the southwestern region of Wales. The mound was the royal site of the old tribal kingdom of Dyfed. It is the scene of much of the Mabinogi. In the tale of Pwyll, the mysterious horsewoman Rhiannon appears on the mound. She cannot be overtaken though her horse seems to walk. In the tale of Manawydan, a mist descends on the mound and takes the people of Dyfed away.
